glossary.Atherosclerotic: Caused by fatty plaques building up in artery walls.
glossary.Peripheral arteries: Arteries outside the heart and brain, mainly those of the legs.
glossary.Limb ischaemia: Inadequate blood supply to an arm or leg.
glossary.Hyperlipidaemia: Raised levels of fats such as cholesterol in the blood.
glossary.Chronic limb ischaemia: Long-standing reduced blood supply to a limb, usually from atherosclerosis.
glossary.Pulselessness: No palpable pulse distal to a blockage.
glossary.Pallor: Unusual paleness of the skin from reduced blood flow.
glossary.Paraesthesia: Pins and needles or tingling from nerve dysfunction.
glossary.Paralysis: Loss of the ability to move a muscle.
glossary.Dangling: Hanging the leg over the bed edge so gravity improves blood flow to the foot.
glossary.PAD: Peripheral arterial disease: atherosclerotic narrowing of the limb arteries.
glossary.Contrast-enhanced: Imaging using an injected dye to make vessels show up clearly.
glossary.Lipids: Blood fats such as cholesterol and triglycerides, checked to assess cardiovascular risk.
glossary.Cardiovascular risk: Chance of heart attack or stroke over a set period.
glossary.Antiplatelets: Drugs that stop platelets clumping, e.g. clopidogrel or aspirin.
glossary.Statins: Cholesterol-lowering drugs that also stabilise plaques.
glossary.Percutaneous transluminal angioplasty: Inflating a balloon inside a narrowed artery via a needle puncture to widen it.
glossary.Conservative management: Treatment without surgery or procedures, e.g. exercise and medicines.
glossary.Revascularisation: Any procedure that restores blood flow to an ischaemic tissue.
glossary.Long-segment lesion: A narrowing that extends over a long length of artery.
glossary.Superimposed infection: Infection developing on top of already damaged tissue.
glossary.Claudication distance: How far a patient can walk before claudication pain starts.
glossary.Oxygen demand: How much oxygen a tissue needs; rises sharply in working muscle.
glossary.Lumen: The hollow inside of a vessel where blood flows.
